correctness.rationale: For binary words using both symbols, the prefix-of-length-|p|-1 earliest-endpoint map is injective for palindromic minimal absent factors. At a hypothetical collision of differing lengths, equal outside letters force the shorter palindrome to occur inside the longer truncated prefix. Different outside letters disallow any next binary letter unless the common endpoint is final, where occurrence of the longer palindrome truncated suffix forces an earlier shorter-prefix occurrence. Monochromatic words have only two minimal absent factors; 01^(n-2)0 realizes n for all n>=3, with n=2 explicitly handled. Independent exhaustive implementations agree and test injection.

originality.rationale: The exact palindromic-subfamily upper bound and the first-occurrence endpoint injection were not located in the inspected primary literature or returned research records. Pinho et al. (2009) and Barton et al. (2014) give general minimal-absent characterizations and algorithms. Almirantis et al. (2017) already gives the same witness for asymptotic tightness, but only exhibits n-2 factors and no sharp palindromic upper bound. A stronger uncatalogued exact full-MAW theorem may still imply the cardinality assertion; this risk is recorded.
residual_risks: A different published exact bound on ALL binary minimal absent factors could imply the present cardinality result with the 2017 witness; no such decisive source was found in the accessible check, so novelty remains a best-knowledge assessment.
A terminological variant such as palindrome-filtered antidictionary may be unindexed.
The published witness has high overlap with the construction; only the exact sharp theorem and first-occurrence injection are presented as new.
